newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian says son died of settler beating.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian says son died of settler beating.

text.p: A 10-year-old Palestinian boy died in a Jerusalem hospital on Monday after being beaten by a Jewish settler who suspected he had thrown stones at Israeli cars, the boy's father said.

Police said Hilmi Shosa collapsed while being chased by the security chief of a Jewish settlement near the West Bank town of Bethlehem on Sunday and there were no external signs on his body that he had been beaten.
The boy's father said the settler landed one blow to his son's head, causing him to fall. He denied his son had thrown stones at Israeli cars.
"The man who beat him said himself to my older son -- he did not know it was my son -- that he hit him and had no idea he would fall like that," Sair Shosa told Israel Radio.
He said his son had been in critical condition overnight and died of his wounds early on Monday. Shosa said an autopsy would be performed.
Police arrested suspect Nahum Kurman, a resident of the West Bank settlement of Efrat.
"I don't believe he caused the death of the boy...I understood he never touched him, that he chased him and the boy fell," said Yoram Kadosh, an official from the nearby Hadar Beitar settlement.
Around 130,000 Jewish settlers live among two million Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, areas Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war.

Israel gave Palestinians limited control over parts of the West Bank after it signed a breakthrough peace agreement with the PLO in 1993 but settlements remain under Israeli control pending a final peace accord.
